result.hw_emu_qemu_boot_detail: qemu reaches Linux kernel boot. MMC controller initialized successfully — kernel sees both partitions: mmcblk0p1 (88064c08-01, 999424 sectors / ~488 MB) AND mmcblk0p2 (88064c08-02, 572416 sectors / ~280 MB). Both partition entries appear in the kernel device list.
result.hw_emu_rootfs_mount_block_reason_root_ca: Kernel tries ALL 8 filesystem drivers in order — ext3, ext2, ext4, cramfs, vfat, msdos, iso9660, btrfs — and EVERY ONE refuses to mount mmcblk0p2. This rules out the original 'wrong partition index / mmcblk0 vs mmcblk1' hypothesis: with BSP-built kernel + board-matched device tree + board-specific boot.scr, the partition is correctly addressed (179,2). The remaining root cause is a SUPERBLOCK / FEATURE mismatch: the Vitis-generated mkfs.ext4 (on the Aliyun ECS host) writes ext4 superblock features (metadata_csum_seed, orphan_file, fast_commit, etc. — enabled by default in e2fsprogs 1.47+) that the PetaLinux 2024.1 kernel's ext4 driver (linux-xlnx 6.6.10) does NOT recognize. Mount fails with 'No filesystem could mount root' on EVERY known filesystem type because none can parse the partition header.
